_readme: Source of truth for the starter roster. Numbers are the third simulator-tuned pass (retuned with the skill library against the authored kits and avatar, with base Speed spread so the fastest beast gets 10-15% more turns than the slowest; see docs/balance/tuning-log.md), not confirmed balance. Edit here, then in Unity run Beast Craft/Data/Import Beast Roster. All species use the medium growth curve for now (user decision); fast and slow are kept, unused, for the balance simulator. Stance is the species' CombatStance (Vanguard, Ranged or Skirmisher; missing means Vanguard), which decides how it positions itself in battle. BaseStats.CritChance is the species' percent critical-hit chance (0-100), used as-is at every level like MoveRange; neither counts toward the six-stat budget. See docs/design/battle-system.md, 'Starter roster' and 'Combat stances'.

Species.Description: A bird of living flame that burns brightest just before it falls. It strikes hard and from afar, and has little to stand behind when the fire is returned.
A serpent of the deep whose coils could cradle a ship. Slow to rise and slower to fall, it outlasts whatever breaks against it.
A hillside that learned to stand. It barely moves and rarely strikes, but nothing gets past it.
Half eagle, half lion, all wind. It is across the field before the enemy has turned, and gone again before the blow lands.
Its wingbeat is the thunder and its dive is the lightning. Nothing acts before it, and little survives its first strike, though it cannot take one back.
An old dragon wrapped in rime. It does not hurry; it simply makes the battlefield colder, and waits for the cold to win.
A patient forest guardian with roots older than kingdoms. It shelters its allies under its boughs and mends what the fight breaks.
A river-beast in a shell of iron plates. Where the Golem only endures, the Tarasque endures and bites back.
A gentle, luminous beast said to walk without bending the grass. It shuns claws and horns, and fights with light instead.
A serpent-king whose gaze reaches farther than any fang. It slips through shadow to find the weakest foe, and cannot afford to be found in turn.
